external_sources.supports: Folding a sheet into a channel can change how it resists bending. The local dimensions, light block test and stop rules are authored classroom choices; no strength result is assumed.

evidence.description: A process record with three authentic stage references/captions, ownership/support notes and a design evaluation linked to an actual result; missing records clearly labelled.
evidence.status: contribution to source assessment; no completion claim

routes.Supported: Supported: match records to stage labels.
routes.Independent: Independent: add what, who and result.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: explain a limit in the evidence.

vocab.definition: The steps used to make something.
Words that explain a picture or record.
Use evidence to judge how well it worked.
Make a change that aims to help.

cases.text: Find your marked plan, card model and actual test record.
cases.next_step: Match each record to plan, build or test.
cases.staff_note: Keep ownership and dates where known; do not invent earlier dates.

cases.text: A photo shows your folded model but no test.
cases.fact: The photo shows the built shape.
cases.next_step: Describe the folds; use the test sheet for test results.
cases.staff_note: Do not infer strength from appearance.

cases.text: An adult helped start a fold.
cases.fact: Part of the making used adult support.
cases.next_step: Write which step the adult helped with.
cases.staff_note: Do not relabel supported work as independent.

cases.next_step: Label the gap and use a real alternative record.
cases.staff_note: A later demonstration is not a record of the original moment.

cases.text: Your test stopped when the model slipped.
cases.fact: The actual test ended at a slip.
cases.next_step: Use that observation to suggest a more secure setup or join.
cases.staff_note: A proposed change is not proven until a fair retest.

cases.text: A photo includes a pupil name or face.
cases.next_step: Ask staff to choose or make a suitable work-only record.
cases.staff_note: Use approved school devices/storage and permissions. Do not publish learner photos from this task.

Purpose and success checks
How can photos and words show what I actually made?
I can select records of my own process. I can add clear and truthful captions. I can use a result to suggest an improvement.

Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries

Do not photograph pupils or personal labels without the setting permissions. No personal devices, public uploads or copied peer evidence. Keep any later demonstration labelled with date and author. Staff handle file/storage steps under local rules.
Assessment and feedback

Check that plan/build/test captions match the supplied work and who did each step. Accept a drawing or work reference when a photo is unavailable, accurately labelled. The evaluation states what worked or did not, cites an observed result and proposes a reasoned change. No fabricated photo, date or load result.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the school's evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Speaking listening and writing
Describe a process step, explain a result and write an evidence-based caption. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own portfolio; no communication criteria are assigned here.

Individual evidence key

Check that plan/build/test captions match the supplied work and who did each step. Accept a drawing or work reference when a photo is unavailable, accurately labelled. The evaluation states what worked or did not, cites an observed result and proposes a reasoned change. No fabricated photo, date or load result.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: Keep ownership and dates where known; do not invent earlier dates.
Card B: Do not infer strength from appearance.
Card C: Do not relabel supported work as independent.
Card D: A later demonstration is not a record of the original moment.
Card E: A proposed change is not proven until a fair retest.
Card F: Use approved school devices/storage and permissions. Do not publish learner photos from this task.
Common misunderstandings
A finished-product photo does not prove every making step. A later demonstration is not earlier evidence. A proposed improvement is not a measured improvement.
Teaching boundary

Do not photograph pupils or personal labels without the setting permissions. No personal devices, public uploads or copied peer evidence. Keep any later demonstration labelled with date and author. Staff handle file/storage steps under local rules.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
